extracted.intended_audience: general readers; journalists; communicators and marketers researching Reddit
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article providing a comprehensive overview of Reddit: its history, features, moderation model, corporate affairs, product changes, community culture, and advertising/PR considerations. Useful as a reference summary of the platform and its norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front-page rank factors
rubrics_metrics.description: "Front-page rank, for both the general front page and for individual subreddits, is determined by a combination of factors, including the age of the submission, positive ('upvoted') to negative ('downvoted') feedback ratio, and the total vote-count."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posts with more upvotes appear towards the top of their subreddit and, if they receive enough upvotes, ultimately on the site's front page (e.g., r/popular). r/popular (and r/all historically) may filter out not-safe-for-work content for unregistered users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subreddit moderation responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: "Moderators are volunteers who manage their communities, set and enforce community-specific rules, remove posts and comments that violate these rules, and often work to keep discussions in their subreddit on topic."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moderators are chosen by creating a subreddit or being promoted; moderator requests are reviewed by Reddit admins for abandoned subreddits. Moderators have broad local control over community norms and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator and enforcement tools (shadowban/suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Early on, Reddit implemented "shadow banning" to address spam accounts; in 2015 Reddit added an account suspension feature which it said would replace sitewide shadowbans, however, moderators are still able to shadowban users or their individual posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement is a mix of automated moderation (bots/automod) and human moderator/admin action; sitewide and subreddit-level enforcement mechanisms coexist and have changed over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subreddit access requirements to deter abuse
rubrics_metrics.description: "Some subreddits have a karma and account age requirement to discourage bots and spammers from posting."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual communities set such gatekeeping thresholds as a quality-control measure; requirements vary by subreddit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post archiving policy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Posts are sometimes automatically archived after six months, meaning they can no longer be commented or voted on."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Archiving limits ongoing interaction on older posts and affects strategies for long-lived discussions or reposting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content-moderation policy aims and banned content
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit instituted policies "aimed at banning content inciting violence and quarantining offensive material," and has had an "anti-harassment policy, banned involuntary sexualization, and banned several forums that focused on bigoted content or harassment of individuals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These platform-level policy changes interact with subreddit-specific rules; transparency reports document removals and reasons. Community reaction can be substantial when policy changes occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency reporting and content-removal metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: "Reddit releases transparency reports annually which have information like how many posts have been taken down by moderators and for what reason." Example: "In 2020, Reddit removed 6% of posts made on the platform (approx. 233 million). More than 99% of removals were marked as spam; the remainder made up of a mix of other offensive content. Around 131 million posts were removed by the automated moderator (~56%) and the rest were taken down manually."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency reports are the main public record for enforcement statistics and are useful to assess moderation scale and causes of removal (spam vs. other violations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Snoo (logo) design restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: When Reddit revamped its website in April 2018, the company imposed several restrictions on how Snoo can be designed: "Snoo's head 'should always appear blank or neutral', Snoo's eyes are orange-red, and Snoo cannot have fingers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit brand/style requirements for permissible uses of the Reddit mascot; many subreddits create customized Snoo variants but must respect these constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising and PR etiquette on Reddit
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for brands: Reddit users "don't want to advertise for you, they want to talk to you." The communities on Reddit "don't want to feel used or exploited. That's where listening comes in."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful brand engagement requires authenticity, transparency, and two-way conversation (e.g., well-run AMAs with honest interaction). Advertisers should be prepared to engage honestly and to accept community criticism; sponsored events and native ads must respect community norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising formats and platform ad features
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit launched sponsored content and a self-serve ads platform in 2009 and has since expanded to promoted headlines, native mobile ads, sponsored AMAs, and other ad formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisers have multiple formats but must tailor approaches to Reddit's community-driven culture; changes to ad offerings (e.g., native ads, mobile-first formats) affect campaign design.

rubrics_metrics.name: User voting and karma as reputation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: "Registered users... submit content... which are then voted up or down ('upvoted' or 'downvoted') by other members... Users can also earn 'karma' for their posts and comments, a status that reflects their standing within the community and their contributions to Reddit."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Karma and vote totals influence visibility and community standing; strategies to earn visibility must consider vote mechanics and community norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and account basics
rubrics_metrics.description: "Registering an account with Reddit is free and requires an email address. Registered users can also create their own subreddit on a topic of their choosing. In Reddit style, usernames begin with 'u/'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic account creation prerequisites and features are minimal, but community acceptance and moderation rules determine what a new account can do (e.g., some subreddits block new accounts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product/feature migration and legacy deprecations
rubrics_metrics.description: The article documents discontinued features and migrations (e.g., free API tier discontinued April 2023; private messaging discontinued in 2025 in favor of Reddit Chat; removal of legacy mobile site i.reddit; feature deprecations on old.reddit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers, third-party app makers, and community managers must track platform changes because API and feature deprecations can abruptly alter workflows, community tools, and user expectations. Such removals have historically provoked strong community backlash.
